chapter: Jules's band and the move north
title: Jules's band goes to New York and 'Dream Alley'
summary: His brother's band plays the Saenger with an MC, goes to New York on promises, and the stranded players share walk-up flats on 47th Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, I was trying to think of the guy's name, uh, this guy was at, uh, a master's ceremony. Mm-hmm. Uh, and he came down and worked at the Strand, uh, not the Strand, but the, the Sanger Theater, the new Sanger at that time was the new Sanger. Uh, from, uh, he was, he was the emceeer of the, of the, of the show, and they had some kind of a, I don't know, some kind of a show, worked out, and my brother's band played with him. Mm-hmm. On the stage, and they had a band in the pit. I think Louis Primo was playing in the pit at that time.

Um, but anyway, uh, they finally, after, after they, after they worked out that, that deal, I think it was about 10 or 12 weeks or something like that that they were there. He, he, like, uh, liked the, the way my brother had the band, and the way he handled the band, and the way it sounded and all, and he thought that, that they should be around in New York, and, and, and do a lot of these, uh, theaters and stuff around in the New England states, you know, and so forth, but, uh, he gave a big bill up on the thing, and, uh, I don't know, when Jules, Jules come on in to New York, I was working with Freddie Rich's band, so I says, so, I, I, I showed him where, where some, some housing was right downtown around Broadway, see, and so forth, and got all the guys set, and he told me what was happening, I said, well, well, if anything goes wrong, I says, we, we can all, we could, get a place together, which later on we did. Mm-hmm. We, we, we got, we finally, when he got in all this trouble and all, before, before he, before he got started, Tony Swain off, was the office that booked the band, see, so, as, as he, as he got everything going, and, and this guy was, give, give him that big bill up, but, but nothing was happening, he was out with his wife on, on, on a yacht somewhere, having a ball, see, so, there, there, these guys, they ain't got no jobs and no money and so forth, so what we all did, we all got together on, on, on 47th Street, and, and one of these walk-up apartments on the top there, I think, and we call it Dream Alley. Mm-hmm. I mean, the first guy that come home at night, he had the bed, see, and then, then they have a, a little bed for all the guys, and this, we had about two or three, two or three different apartments there, see, and I moved in with them, see, and, and then, anyway, Lefty Hyman was with the bed, he'll tell you about all the lefties going on, but, but, uh, they had, they had all, all, all that, all that bunch of, a bunch of things, and, I, I, I don't, I don't know how to explain it, but, uh, we had a ball there for a while, and finally, finally some of the guys got homesick, and, and, and bands kind of split up, see, after they did, they did a lot, a lot of water building, and stuff like that, but then the band, so Jules, uh, finally, finally, he, he, he went, went to work at the Rudy Vallée office, see, and I'm trying to figure that that violin player was with Rudy Vallée, anyway, Jules worked with him for a while, so, I, I can't think of all the names right now.
